files.path: ripple blockchain pastcode/ripple blockchain/final code/python/current fetch/current transaction fetch.py
files.folder: ripple blockchain pastcode/ripple blockchain/final code/python/current fetch
files.role: legacy script (old code, kept for reference, not maintained)
files.purpose: The most complete legacy LIVE-FOLLOW (tail) script: reads all settings from .env, keeps a checkpoint of the last processed ledger in MongoDB, polls the server for new validated ledgers and saves each ledger, its transactions and their meta/memos. A stop file (current_process=0) ends it.
files.how: setup_mongodb_indexes() -> fetch_current_transactions_loop(): get_last_processed_ledger_index(), connect_xrpl(), loop: get_process_status(), get_latest_validated_ledger_index(), _process_single_ledger_with_transactions() for each new ledger (save_to_mongo ledger -> transactions -> meta), update_last_processed_ledger_index().

functions.does: Creates indexes: unique block_number on ledgers, unique sparse hash on transactions, unique sparse transaction_hash on meta, plus lookup indexes. Errors are only logged.

functions.does: Live-follow loop: every few seconds asks for the newest ledger and processes every ledger after the last processed one.

external_resources: env vars: MONGO_URI, DB_NAME, LEDGER_COLLECTION, TX_COLLECTION, META_MEMOS_COLLECTION, FAILED_TX_COLLECTION, METADATA_COLLECTION, SERVERS, MAX_RETRIES, REQUEST_TIMEOUT, POLLING_INTERVAL_SECONDS, RECONNECT_DELAY_BASE, PROCESS_STATUS_FILE
.env in the current folder (load_dotenv) -- the legacy .env exists but was NOT read (it holds a real MongoDB URI)
stop file PROCESS_STATUS_FILE (process_status.txt next to it)
notes: Reads settings at import time; int(os.getenv(...)) crashes with TypeError if a variable is missing from .env.
Failure-record bug: {'$set': failed_entry, '$inc': {'retry_count': 1}} sets AND increments retry_count in one update -> MongoDB rejects it (conflict), so failed ledgers are never recorded.
On a timeout in every attempt, ledger_data / num_transactions / close_time were never assigned -> UnboundLocalError when the failure is recorded.
Any other exception does 'break' and the function returns None (not False); the caller then treats it as failure and reconnects, retrying the same ledger forever if it keeps failing.
Ledger document is written BEFORE its transactions, so a crash in between leaves a ledger that looks complete but has no transactions.
Opens a new MongoClient for every save.
Stop file: only the first line is read.
Uses xrpl-py (AsyncWebsocketClient), which the new package intentionally does not use.

notes: Byte-for-byte identical copy of 'current fetch/current transaction fetch.py' (same MD5).
Reads settings at import time; int(os.getenv(...)) crashes with TypeError if a variable is missing from .env.
Failure-record bug: {'$set': failed_entry, '$inc': {'retry_count': 1}} sets AND increments retry_count in one update -> MongoDB rejects it (conflict), so failed ledgers are never recorded.
On a timeout in every attempt, ledger_data / num_transactions / close_time were never assigned -> UnboundLocalError when the failure is recorded.
Any other exception does 'break' and the function returns None (not False); the caller then treats it as failure and reconnects, retrying the same ledger forever if it keeps failing.
Ledger document is written BEFORE its transactions, so a crash in between leaves a ledger that looks complete but has no transactions.
Opens a new MongoClient for every save.
Stop file: only the first line is read.
Uses xrpl-py (AsyncWebsocketClient), which the new package intentionally does not use.

Database 'xrpl_data', 8 processes.
files.how: get_ledger_range() -> bulk_fetch_ledgers(): Pool(initializer=worker_init).map(_worker_fetch_only_ledgers) -> sleep 10 s -> read ledgers back from MongoDB -> Pool.map(_worker_fetch_and_process_transactions) -> _process_transactions_for_ledger() -> fetch_transactions() / process_transactions() / save_to_mongo() -> Phase 3 loop Pool.map(_worker_fetch_and_process_transactions_for_retry).

functions.name: get_ledger_range
functions.does: Asks on the keyboard for start and end ledger (start must be >= 32570, start <= end).

functions.name: connect_xrpl
functions.does: Tries each server in SERVERS up to MAX_RETRIES times with xrpl-py AsyncWebsocketClient.
functions.output: open client; raises if every server fails

functions.name: fetch_ledger
functions.does: Fetches one ledger header (copies differ: with or without transactions); returns {} after all retries fail.

functions.name: fetch_transactions
functions.does: Fetches one ledger with expanded transactions; returns [] after all retries fail.

functions.name: process_transactions
functions.does: Turns raw transactions into flat transaction documents (field renames, tx_json flattened, simple type casts) and separate meta/memo documents. Exact rules differ per script.
functions.inputs: block_number: int, block_hash: str, close_time: int, transactions: List[Dict]

functions.name: apply_renames_to_doc
functions.does: Applies FIELD_RENAMES to a document's keys (in M5/TR2 copies it only adds _inserted_at despite its name).

functions.name: save_to_mongo
functions.does: Saves to one collection: ledgers are upserted by ledger number, transactions and meta are bulk-inserted with insert_many (exact rules differ per script).

functions.name: worker_init
functions.does: Pool initializer: creates one MongoClient per worker process (global variables).

functions.name: _process_only_ledger_batch
functions.does: Phase 1 helper: fetches ledger headers (and tx counts) for a range and saves them.
functions.inputs: client: AsyncWebsocketClient, start_ledger: int, end_ledger: int

functions.name: _worker_fetch_only_ledgers
functions.does: Phase 1 worker process: fetches ledger headers for its range and saves them.

functions.name: _process_transactions_for_ledger
functions.does: Phase 2: fetches the transactions of one stored ledger and saves transactions + meta (newer copies record failures).

functions.name: _worker_fetch_and_process_transactions
functions.does: Phase 2 worker process: runs _process_transactions_for_ledger for its batch of ledgers.

functions.name: _process_transactions_for_retry
functions.does: Retry phase: re-fetches one failed ledger's transactions; on success deletes it from the failed collection.

functions.name: _worker_fetch_and_process_transactions_for_retry
functions.does: Retry-phase worker process for a batch of failed ledgers.

functions.name: bulk_fetch_ledgers
functions.does: Splits the range across NUM_PROCESSES worker processes (multiprocessing.Pool) and runs the phases of the bulk download.

external_resources: URLs in code: mongodb://localhost:27017, wss://s.altnet.rippletest.net:51233, wss://s2.ripple.com, wss://xrplcluster.com
keyboard prompts: Enter the end ledger number: | Enter the start ledger number:
notes: Byte-for-byte identical copy of 'multiprocess 5 complete.py' (same MD5).
Phase 3 'while True' never ends if one ledger can never be fetched (endless retry loop).
Phase 1 failures (ledger header not fetched) are only logged, never recorded: those ledgers are missing for good.
insert_many without unique indexes: running the same range again stores duplicate transactions/meta.
logging.FileHandler('xrpl_fetcher.log', 'w') empties the log file on every start.
A new client opened inside fetch_ledger/fetch_transactions after a drop is a local variable: it is never closed and never handed back, so the caller keeps passing the closed one.
fetch_ledger() and _process_only_ledger_batch() are defined but never called (Phase 1 worker inlines the request).
apply_renames_to_doc() does no renaming here (only adds _inserted_at) despite its name.
All settings are hard-coded in the file (MongoDB URI, database, servers, retries).
SERVERS mixes mainnet with the TESTNET server wss://s.altnet.rippletest.net:51233: on failover it can store testnet data as if it were mainnet.
No stop file and no resume: a stopped run starts again from the typed range.
Uses xrpl-py (AsyncWebsocketClient), which the new package intentionally does not use.

notes: Differs from 'multiprocess 6 complete.py' only in the DB name (2 diff lines).
A ledger that fails all retries is skipped silently (fetch returns {} / []), so it is missing from MongoDB without any record.
Phase 2 cannot tell 'empty ledger' from 'fetch failed': failed transaction fetches are not recorded.
insert_many without unique indexes: running the same range again stores duplicate transactions/meta.
All settings are hard-coded in the file (MongoDB URI, database, servers, retries).
SERVERS mixes mainnet with the TESTNET server wss://s.altnet.rippletest.net:51233: on failover it can store testnet data as if it were mainnet.
No stop file and no resume: a stopped run starts again from the typed range.
Uses xrpl-py (AsyncWebsocketClient), which the new package intentionally does not use.

files.purpose: Edits the xrpld node config file (xrpld.cfg) so the node keeps full history (or a pruned window), uses the chosen database path and size, and opens the local admin websocket port 6006 that the ingester connects to. It backs the file up first and writes it atomically, and running it twice gives the same result.

End-to-end: real spawn process pool + real websockets + real MongoDB.

Uses a throwaway database `xrpl_ingest_test_<uuid>` that is dropped afterwards; no other
database is touched and `.env` is never loaded (the Config is built here). Skipped when
MongoDB does not answer a ping within 1s, or when XRPL_INGEST_NO_INTEGRATION=1.
Run only these: `python -m pytest -m integration`.

files.docstring:
Every value the node sends must be recoverable from what we store.

Mapping (documented in transform.py): a ledger's header fields and result-level fields go
to the ledger doc; each transaction's outer fields and tx_json fields go to its tx doc; its
meta is stored whole in the meta doc. Mapped fields keep their names (FIELD_RENAMES /
LEDGER_RENAMES) and int coercion; everything else is stored as received under its own name,
or under raw_<key> when that name already holds a different value. Keys are escaped
('.' -> '．', NUL -> '␀', leading '$' -> '＄').

files.purpose: Downloads old ledger history (backfill). It asks the node which ledgers it has, cuts the requested range into chunks of CHUNK_SIZE ledgers, skips chunks already finished, and runs the chunks in several worker processes at once. It also holds retry-failed, which downloads again the ledgers in the failed collection.
files.how: run_backfill(): checks free disk, creates indexes, calls discover_node(), plans chunks with ledger_ranges.plan_chunks(), then _run_pool() runs _run_chunk_in_process() in a spawn ProcessPoolExecutor (one chunk per process at a time). Each worker runs process_chunk(): CONCURRENCY async workers call fetcher.ingest_ledger() for each ledger, then the chunk is marked done in MongoDB. The parent checks the stop file, signals and disk every second and tells workers to stop through a shared Event. retry_failed() retries failed ledgers in rounds; ledgers that failed because the connection was lost are retried one at a time, last.

files.purpose: Defines every error type the program raises and decides which errors are worth retrying. Temporary problems (timeouts, lost connection, ledger not validated yet, MongoDB errors, some node error codes) are retried; permanent ones (wrong network, broken ledger data, unknown ledger, a stop request) are not.
files.how: A class tree under IngestError: ConfigError, TransientError (ConnectFailed -> StopRequested, ConnectionLost, RequestTimeout, NotValidated), NetworkMismatch, MalformedLedger and RpcError (holds the node's error code). RETRYABLE_RPC_ERRORS lists node error codes that are temporary. is_retryable() is the one place that decides retry or not.

files.purpose: Downloads, converts and saves ONE ledger, with retries. If the ledger still fails after all retries, it is written into the failed-ledgers collection so it can be retried later. Both backfill and tail use it.

files.purpose: Checks that the stored data is complete and can fix it. It finds missing ledgers and ledgers with the wrong number of transactions; with --deep it also checks that each ledger links to the one before it (parent hash) and compares stored transaction hashes with the node. With --repair it downloads the bad ledgers again. It also compares one stored transaction with the node for the `tx` command.
files.how: repair_range() goes through the range in windows of 10,000 ledgers (so memory stays small). _check_window() collects problems from store.py; compare_hashes() asks the node for each ledger's hash list (fetch_hashes, with retries). _repair_window() re-ingests the bad ledgers the node has with ingest_many() (fetcher.ingest_ledger, clear_failure=True) and checks the window again. No chunk is marked; extra stored transactions are only reported, never deleted.

files.docstring:
verify --repair / --deep: find bad ledgers in a stored range and (optionally) re-ingest them.
Also the pure comparison behind `tx --hash` (stored tx vs node, at the end).

Checks, window by window (VERIFY_WINDOW ledgers, so memory stays bounded for any range):
- always: missing ledger documents (gaps) and stored tx count != num_transactions;
- deep, offline: ledger N's parent_hash == stored block_hash of N-1 (when N-1 is stored);
- deep, with node: stored tx hashes of each ledger == the node's `ledger` hash list
  (transactions, expand=false), one ledger at a time.
Repair re-ingests exactly the missing, count-mismatch and (deep) hash-mismatch ledgers the node
has, through ingest_ledger(clear_failure=True) like retry-failed, then checks the window again.
No chunk is ever marked. Extra stored tx docs are reported, never deleted.

files.purpose: Talks to your xrpld node over a websocket. It sends JSON requests (ledger, server_info, tx), waits for the matching answers, reconnects when the connection drops, tries the next server in the list, and refuses a node that reports a different network (for example testnet).
files.how: WsSource keeps one websocket (_Conn) and many requests in flight at once; each request has an id and a Future, and _read_loop hands each answer to the request with the same id. _open() tries every server several times with growing waits (RetryPolicy from fetcher.py) and checks network_id. A request that times out only drops the connection if nothing at all arrived during the timeout (hung socket). Error answers become RpcError; node 'warnings' are kept with the result.

files.purpose: Follows the node live: every few seconds it asks for the newest validated ledger and saves every new ledger in order. It remembers where it stopped (checkpoint) so a restart continues there.
files.how: tail() loops until a stop is requested: asks source.latest_validated(), then calls fetcher.ingest_ledger() for each ledger after the checkpoint and saves the checkpoint. With no checkpoint it starts after the highest stored ledger if that is within 1000 ledgers, else at the current ledger (and logs the backfill command for the hole). A failure that could not even be recorded keeps the checkpoint and retries after a wait.

files.purpose: Implements the `doctor` and `config` commands. doctor checks everything before you start: Python and package versions, the settings, file paths, free disk and RAM, MongoDB (reachable, version 7/8, login, free disk, index conflicts in an old database, chunk marks from another CHUNK_SIZE) and the node (sync state, network, ledgers, peers). config prints every setting with where it came from.

Index conflicts are found by letting MongoStore.ensure_indexes() 'create' its indexes on a fake object (_Recorder) to learn what it wants, then comparing with the real database. Network calls use 5-second timeouts (fast_store/fast_source from monitor.py).

Files people edit: .env lookup + base dir, BOM/UTF-16-safe decoding, and
backfill_range.txt (the default backfill range).

textfile.py (merged): Small text files written by people and Windows tools: .env, stop file, range file.

Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes UTF-16LE with BOM for `>` / Out-File and UTF-8 with BOM for
`Set-Content -Encoding utf8`; Notepad may write either. All of them must read the same as
a plain UTF-8 file.

paths.py (merged): Where things are: the base directory, the .env file, and relative paths.

Rules (see README):
- `.env` is `ENV_FILE` if set, else `<XRPL_INGEST_HOME or cwd>/.env`. No walking up the tree.
- base dir = `XRPL_INGEST_HOME` (process env, or set inside the .env), else the directory of
  the loaded .env, else the current directory. Relative paths in the config (stop file, range
  file, log file, lock files, MONGO_URI_FILE) resolve against it.
- Process environment variables win over values in the .env file.

rangefile.py (merged): backfill_range.txt: the default range for `backfill` (and `status` progress).

    # used by `backfill` when neither --start nor --end is given
    start = 32570
    end   = latest      # or a ledger number

One `key = value` per line; blank and `#` lines ignored, inline ` #` comments allowed; keys
case-insensitive, only `start` and `end`. start: digits (underscores allowed) or `first`
(= 32570), >= 32570, default 32570. end: digits or `latest` (default), >= start. Decoded like
.env (UTF-8 / UTF-8-BOM / UTF-16-BOM), at most 4096 bytes. Read once; never written.

files.docstring:
Run control: graceful stop (stop file + signals) and one instance per command (lock).

stopflag.py (merged): Graceful stop: the stop file (process_status.txt) and signals.

Stop file: any line whose key matters to this command and whose value is 0 stops it; keys
are case-insensitive. `current_process=0` stops every command, `tail=0`, `backfill=0` and
`retry-failed=0` stop only that command; any other value (e.g. `=1`) means keep running.
Blank lines, `#` comments and other keys are skipped. A missing or unreadable file means
keep running (legacy behaviour).

Signals: SIGTERM (e.g. `systemctl stop`) and SIGBREAK (Windows Ctrl+Break) act like the
stop file. With install_stop_signal(graceful_sigint=True) the first Ctrl+C (SIGINT) does too
and the second one aborts at once (KeyboardInterrupt, exit 130).

lock.py (merged): One running instance per command: an OS file lock on <base>/xrpl_ingest.<command>.lock.

POSIX: fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) on the whole file. Windows: msvcrt.locking(LK_NBLCK)
on one byte far past the end, so the holder info written at the start stays readable for
the process that is refused. The OS drops the lock when the holder exits or dies, so a
leftover file is harmless (it only keeps the last holder's info); it is never deleted.

startup.title: Start-up
startup.text: Every command starts the same way: read the command line, load .env, build and check the settings, start logging, install the stop handlers. tail / backfill / retry-failed also get a StopFlag (stop file) and a one-copy-only lock file. doctor and config keep going with broken settings so they can report them.

fetch.title: Fetch one ledger from the node
fetch.text: For each ledger number, fetcher.ingest_ledger asks the node (through WsSource) for the full ledger with every transaction expanded. One websocket connection carries many requests at once; answers are matched by id. A dropped connection reconnects or fails over to the next server.

steps.does: Asks for one ledger with all transactions expanded.

steps.data: tries each server in SERVERS; rejects a server whose network_id is not EXPECTED_NETWORK_ID
steps.does: Tries each server several times; checks the network; stops early if a stop was requested; raises NetworkMismatch if every server is on the wrong network, else …

steps.data: sends the request with an id, waits for the answer with that id (REQUEST_TIMEOUT)
steps.does: Sends one request on a connection and waits for its answer with a timeout; turns error answers into RpcError.

convert.title: Convert to MongoDB documents
convert.text: transform.py turns the raw answer into 3 kinds of documents without losing any field: one ledger document, one transaction document per transaction, one meta document per transaction.
